blogs.title: When 'Endometriomas' Aren't: Deciphering Atypical Myomas in Pregnancy via Non-Contrast MRI
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic dilemma of distinguishing between decidualized endometriomas and giant, cystic-degenerating leiomyomas in the second trimester. We analyze why standard tumor markers like CA-125 can be misleading in pregnancy and demonstrate how non-contrast MRI serves as the critical tie-breaker when ultrasound findings are equivocal regarding mass origin and vascularity.

blogs.title: The Art of Partial Myomectomy: Why Leaving Masses Behind Can Save a Pregnancy
blogs.description: Focusing on surgical strategy, this article discusses the high-stakes decision-making process of performing a targeted resection versus leaving a complex pelvic mass *in situ*. We examine the specific criteria for intervention—such as torsion, necrosis, and mechanical obstruction—and argue why minimizing operative trauma by removing only the symptomatic pedunculated mass preserved both maternal health and fetal viability in this case.

blogs.title: Beyond Expectant Management: Navigating Acute Complications of Large Uterine Fibroids During Gestation
blogs.description: While most fibroid pregnancies are managed conservatively, this post highlights red flags that mandate urgent surgical intervention. Using the case of a twisted, ischemic pedunculated myoma causing severe pain and dyspnea, we review the indications for mid-trimester laparotomy, including impending rupture, infection risk, and mechanical compromise of maternal cardiopulmonary function.

blogs.title: Obstetric Planning with Giant Pelvic Masses: To Deliver Vaginally or Cut?
blogs.description: This entry addresses the long-term obstetric implications of retaining large posterior cervical or isthmic myomas. We discuss how mass location dictates the mode of delivery, analyzing why an elective Cesarean section became inevitable despite successful mid-trimester surgery, and reviewing data on how myoma size correlates with preterm labor risks and delivery timing.

blogs.title: Physiological vs. Pathological: Interpreting Rising CA-125 Levels in Pregnant Patients with Adnexal Masses
blogs.description: A deep dive into biomarker interpretation during pregnancy. With CA-125 known to fluctuate physiologically across trimesters, this post provides guidance on interpreting serial elevations in the context of suspected malignancy versus benign pathology like leiomyomas or endometriosis, helping clinicians avoid unnecessary panic while maintaining vigilance for true neoplasms.
